GAUNTLET-0.failure_condition: no render phase reaches 500 permille (no single-phase optimization is justified; the 'incremental floor cast' hypothesis specifically dies unless frame() >= 500 permille); or the phase times do not reconcile with the render total; or the shape is not reproducible on a second run; or the breakdown rendered anything other than the frozen witnesses
interpretation_limits: host-CPU-specific absolute times; the p99 render-share (permille) is the portable quantity, not the microseconds

GAUNTLET-1.hypothesis: emit is GAUNTLET-1's target (from GAUNTLET-0). A candidate emit is ACCEPTED as a renderer iff it is byte-identical to the frozen mantle.rs emit (pixel_sha) with an unchanged frame (frame_digest) over the corpus PLUS adversarial cameras; correctness is mandatory and independent of speed. A candidate is PROMOTED to the fast path iff it is accepted AND measurably faster on ONE consistent apparatus; identical-but-slower is a correctness pass and a performance fail; different pixels is not a renderer at any speed
GAUNTLET-1.success_condition: gauntlet1-equiv PASSES (fast_pixels == pixels and fast_frame == frame over every corpus and adversarial case); gauntlet1-region names the dominant divide-work region deterministically; and a promotion is claimed only with byte-identity AND a same-apparatus host speed measurement (witnesses checked first) against a stated threshold, sealed off-gate as GAUNTLET-1b citing this entry
GAUNTLET-1.failure_condition: any case where fast_equal != OK, or fast_pixels != pixels, or fast_frame != frame, refuses the candidate as a renderer regardless of speed; a promotion claimed without byte-identity, or without a same-apparatus speed measurement, or by comparing against GAUNTLET-0's instrumented render absolute; or mantle.rs is modified (the reference must stay frozen)
interpretation_limits: mantle.rs is the frozen correctness oracle: the differential compares candidate -> frozen, never the reverse, and the harness is not the oracle; the candidate is guilty until its bytes agree
correctness (byte-identity) and performance (speed) are two SEPARATE courts; byte-identity is mandatory and gate-enforced, speed is judged independently off-gate
the region measure is divide-work (a source-derived proxy: ceiling 0, wall 1, floor 4 integer divisions per pixel), NOT a wall-clock; it names a target, it is not a speedup
a GAUNTLET-1b speed number is host-specific and is NEVER compared to GAUNTLET-0's instrumented render absolute (different apparatus); it is a same-apparatus frozen-vs-candidate delta
GAUNTLET-1a commits NO optimization technique; the seed fast.rs is an exact transcription that only proves the harness

RE-BREAKDOWN-1.hypothesis: After GAUNTLET-1c the emit cost structure shifted (a 536x floor divide cut bought ~12% wall-clock), so the next step is to MEASURE, not optimize. emit's internal cost is attributed two ways: Court A, a DETERMINISTIC structural measure (gate-enforced, wall-clock-free) of what work exists; and Court B, a host ablation of fenced probes (addr -> lookup -> full) timed against emit. The probes are MEASUREMENT APPARATUS, NOT candidate renderers: a probe may be wrong by construction provided its wrongness is isolated from the certified path and its work is a demonstrable subset of that path (proven by probe VERIFY == emit, byte-identical).
RE-BREAKDOWN-1.success_condition: Court A passes on gate: emitbd_verify OK (the probe VERIFY path is byte-identical to emit and the frozen witness), write coverage is exactly once over every framebuffer pixel, and the memory reads are 3 per textured pixel; the working-set cardinality and the floor texel-stride locality are reported as data. Court B is a same-apparatus host ablation sealed off-gate as verdandi-emit-breakdown citing this entry, with the deltas read as incremental attribution.
RE-BREAKDOWN-1.failure_condition: probe VERIFY != emit (the apparatus is not a subset of the certified path); or the production emit or emit_collapse calls a probe (the fence is breached); or a Court B delta is interpreted as a pure hardware-resource cost rather than an incremental ablation delta; or any optimization is committed on this rung before the number (RE-BREAKDOWN-1 measures, it does not optimize); or a Court B number is compared to GAUNTLET-0's instrumented render absolute.
interpretation_limits: RE-BREAKDOWN-1 MEASURES, it does not optimize: no candidate renderer is committed on this rung
Court A and Court B are two separate courts; Court A is a source-derived proxy for time (deterministic, gate-enforced), Court B is the wall-clock (host, off-gate)

the Court B deltas (LOOKUP-ADDR, FULL-LOOKUP) are incremental wall-clock attribution under controlled ablation, NOT pure hardware-resource measurements; cache state, branches, scheduling and register pressure make the subtraction non-additive; the experiment possesses no architectural counters
the probes are measurement apparatus, not renderers: they never enter fast.rs's promotion chain, the production emit calls none of them, and a differing probe pixel is expected, not a fault
a Court B number is host-specific and is NEVER compared to GAUNTLET-0's instrumented render absolute (different apparatus)

the promotion rule is locked before any result: lookup increment or pathological locality -> LOCK a data-layout/locality court; address/DDA -> arithmetic path; full-write -> framebuffer path; results disagree or nothing dominates -> DEFER, do not optimize by intuition

LOCALITY-0.hypothesis: RE-BREAKDOWN-1b named the tile fetch as emit's leading cost (clean ~4.4x over the map indirection). A cache-friendlier floor-tile EXECUTION FORMAT reduces that stall while producing byte-identical pixels. Two layouts compete, each a lossless bijection: BLOCKED (8x8 cache blocks, cheap shift/mask index) and MORTON (Z-order curve, portable scalar bit-interleave, a larger index tax). The winner is the one with the lower net p99 (memory saving Y minus its index-arithmetic tax X) on a process-isolated same-apparatus court; it LOCKs the data-layout court. Content provenance is isolated from execution format: the swizzle is a pure re-format, never a content edit.
LOCALITY-0.success_condition: locality0-equiv PASSES: both layouts byte-identical to the frozen emit over corpus + adversarial cameras AND on a non-vacuous synthetic distinct-per-texel render (mandatory, gate-enforced); each swizzle is a lossless bijection (locality0-bijection, proven on distinct data); the canonical-order content hash is unmoved while the storage layout moves (locality0-provenance); and a layout is promoted only with byte-identity AND a lower process-isolated p99 than the DDA baseline (4734 us p99 on the host), sealed off-gate as LOCALITY-0 citing this entry, with the accepted single-thread emit sealed as the GAUNTLET-2 baseline.
LOCALITY-0.failure_condition: any layout not byte-identical to the frozen emit (a regression) refuses it; a swizzle that moves the tile CONTENT (unswizzled hash changes) rather than only the format; a speed claim from separately-run (non-interleaved) invocations, or compared to GAUNTLET-0's instrumented render absolute; or a layout committed to the accepted path without byte-identity AND a same-apparatus win over the DDA baseline.
interpretation_limits: the Epistemic-Invariance boundary: variants are monomorphized and hot-swapped at the binary boundary, process-isolated per invocation, and interleaved to cancel drift; instruction-level invariance up to address-generation is a structuring goal, NOT gate-provable — the gate proves OUTPUT byte-identity, and the record says so
correctness (byte-identity) is mandatory and gate-enforced; speed is a SEPARATE host court, process-isolated, judged against the DDA baseline (4734 us) — never GAUNTLET-0's instrumented absolute
the per-band wall-clock deltas are host measurements; the per-band within-cache-line locality is a deterministic source-cost proxy, not a wall-clock
content provenance is isolated from execution format: the swizzle moves the layout, not the certified content (the text-reformat law applied to the tile)

three exits: BLOCKED wins, MORTON wins, or NEITHER beats the baseline — the last is not a null but a proof the tile-fetch stall is a capacity/LRU miss no permutation fixes, redirecting to GAUNTLET-2 (parallelism) to hide the latency behind compute

the accepted single-thread emit is sealed as the HARD BASELINE for GAUNTLET-2; the emit stays embarrassingly parallel (per-column wall, per-row floor, only the per-row DDA recurrence, independent across rows)

GAUNTLET-2.hypothesis: LOCALITY-0 LOCKED the blocked floor-tile layout as the accepted single-thread emit and sealed its process-isolated p99 as the hard baseline. GAUNTLET-2 does NOT merely 'make emit multithreaded'; it establishes the stronger property that PARTITIONING THE COLUMN DOMAIN changes execution parallelism but not the certified picture. The law: emit over any partition of the columns into groups, processed in any order, across any admitted thread count T, is byte-identical to the frozen emit — thread count and column partition are EXECUTION parameters, not rendering authority. A candidate is ACCEPTED iff byte-invariant over every admitted (T, partition); it is PROMOTED iff its host p99 beats the sealed single-thread baseline at some admitted T greater than 1. The emit is embarrassingly parallel by construction, so parallelism hides the tile-fetch latency behind compute; it does not remove the capacity/LRU stall.
GAUNTLET-2.success_condition: TWO COURTS. Correctness (deterministic, gate-enforced): a partition-agnostic emit reproduces the frozen frame_digest AND pixel_sha for every tested column partition — contiguous chunks at T in {1,2,4,8,16}, AND adversarial partitions (strided/interleaved column assignment, reversed processing order, single-column groups, and a seeded permutation) — over the corpus plus adversarial cameras; the output bytes are invariant across all of them. Performance (host, off-gate): a threaded emit (std::thread, no crates) partitions the columns across an EXPLICIT thread count T that is an input to the benchmark and is recorded in the attestation (a T | correctness | p99 matrix), witnesses checked before any number; a promotion is claimed only with byte-identity AND a same-apparatus host p99 strictly below the sealed LOCALITY-0 single-thread baseline at some admitted T greater than 1, sealed off-gate citing this entry.
GAUNTLET-2.failure_condition: any (T, partition) where the picture differs from the frozen emit or from the T=1 contiguous result refuses the candidate regardless of speed — that is a partition or order dependency (shared framebuffer state, shared temporary state, mutable material-lookup state, column ordering, thread-local initialization, or reduction/merge ordering); a promotion claimed without byte-identity, without the explicit recorded thread count, without a same-apparatus measurement, or by comparing against GAUNTLET-0's instrumented render absolute or the old frozen renderer instead of the sealed single-thread baseline; or mantle.rs is modified; or the single-thread baseline is re-derived on this rung rather than inherited from the sealed LOCALITY-0 record.
interpretation_limits: the single-thread baseline is INHERITED from LOCALITY-0's sealed accepted-emit p99 (the LOCKED blocked emit), never re-measured on this rung; GAUNTLET-2 must beat that exact hard floor, not a fresh number

PARTITION INVARIANCE is the core property: the certified picture is byte-invariant under EVERY admitted column partition and processing order, not merely under thread count — thread count and partition are execution parameters, not rendering authority; adversarial partitions (strided/interleaved, reversed order, single-column groups, a seeded permutation) are tested, never merely contiguous chunks; thread-count invariance is the special case of contiguous partitions at T = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16
byte-identity is mandatory and gate-enforced; correctness (the deterministic partition-invariance proof) and speed (the host threaded p99) are two separate courts, judged independently
T is an EXPLICIT thread count, an input to the benchmark recorded in the attestation (the T | correctness | p99 matrix), never selected implicitly by the runtime

the decision rule is preregistered BEFORE THE NUMBER: promote the parallel emit iff it is byte-invariant AND some admitted T greater than 1 has p99 below the sealed baseline; if p99 stops improving as T grows (sublinear or negative scaling), that is evidence of memory-bandwidth / cache contention, not insufficient parallelism, and the trajectory turns to the memory hierarchy rather than blindly increasing T

a GAUNTLET-2 speed number is host-specific and is NEVER compared to GAUNTLET-0's instrumented render absolute, nor to the old frozen renderer, nor made into an absolute refresh-rate claim; it is a same-apparatus parallel-vs-sealed-single-thread delta

the emit is embarrassingly parallel by construction (per-column wall, per-row floor, the per-row DDA recurrence independent across rows); parallelism HIDES the tile-fetch latency behind compute, it does not remove the capacity/LRU stall that LOCALITY-0's third exit named

LATENCY-1.hypothesis: GAUNTLET-2 LOCKED the T=8 threaded emit as the production render (~3.3x faster emit, byte-identical) and the shell now renders through it. LATENCY-1 asks — to be MEASURED, never assumed — whether replacing the renderer with that promoted T=8 path measurably changes the frame-ready -> composited latency of the fixed sealed playback sequence, versus the LATENCY-0 sealed baseline. It does NOT ask whether rendering is faster (that is already established); it asks whether the render headroom propagates into the measured presentation path or whether presentation/DWM remains the dominant measured boundary.
LATENCY-1.success_condition: on the host, replaying the SAME sealed reference session through the SAME apparatus as LATENCY-0 (shell playback-window --measure), but with the promoted T=8 threaded renderer, a record of per-frame frame-ready -> composited p50/p95/p99/max us sealed under the envelope with the measured refresh period beside it, witnesses checked first; the comparison is drawn ONLY against the LATENCY-0 sealed frame-ready -> composited baseline (the SAME observable), inherited from shell/attest/latency-<host>.json and never re-derived.
LATENCY-1.failure_condition: comparing the LATENCY-1 number against any observable other than LATENCY-0's sealed frame-ready -> composited baseline — in particular against an emit p99 (the GAUNTLET-2 7734 us baseline is an emit p99, a DIFFERENT observable, and using it is a category error); a claim of input-to-photon latency; no composited timestamp readable from DWM on the host; the shape not reproducible on a second run; the baseline re-derived rather than inherited from the sealed LATENCY-0 record; or the sealed session or the measurement apparatus changed from LATENCY-0's (then it is not the same experiment).
interpretation_limits: the comparator is LATENCY-0's sealed frame-ready -> composited p99, NOT an emit p99: they are DIFFERENT observables (a render-phase time versus a present-path time) and must never be mixed; only the same-observable, same-apparatus delta is legitimate
the single-thread render baseline is INHERITED from the sealed LATENCY-0 record (shell/attest/latency-<host>.json), never re-derived on this rung

the disciplined reading of the delta: an IMPROVEMENT means the renderer headroom is propagating into the measured presentation path; NO MATERIAL improvement means presentation/DWM remains the dominant measured boundary; a DEGRADATION means the threaded path introduced a new scheduling/contention cost at the shell boundary; NONE of these by itself proves input-to-photon latency

frame-ready -> composited excludes the kernel render (that is the bench), input transport, the present wait beyond composition, and the panel scan-out; it is NOT input-to-photon (that needs capture hardware)

the promoted T=8 render's per-frame thread-spawn cost is UPSTREAM of frame-ready (it is part of producing the frame, not of presenting it), so it does not enter this observable directly; a render regression would show only insofar as it delays frame-ready
Windows-only; off-gate on a named host; the sequence is the fixed sealed reference session, not arbitrary interactive load

This amendment does not alter LATENCY-1's observable, comparator, session, apparatus or entry; it binds how LATENCY-1's delta may be read.

LATENCY-1R.hypothesis: Whether GAUNTLET-2's render headroom reaches composited output — MEASURED, never assumed. On the same sealed reference session and the same GDI window present (StretchDIBits + DwmFlush, QPC), a render-INCLUSIVE interval, render-start -> composited, is timed per sample for two arms rendering the identical certified frame: PRODUCTION (fast::render, emit_threaded at PROD_THREADS = 8) and the SINGLE-THREAD reference (the LOCKED single-thread fast::emit over the same frozen strips + frame, the same HUD overlay and the same blit conversion). The render's phase relative to composition is a declared variable with two regimes: LOCKED (the render starts immediately after a composition) and UNIFORM (the render starts at a pseudo-random offset uniform in [0, refresh) after a composition, from the fixed seed 0x5EED1A7E00000001). LATENCY-0 established that this present is refresh-coupled, which predicts that in LOCKED a render that already fits one refresh gains little at the glass while in UNIFORM the gain approaches the render delta; both are to be measured, not assumed.
LATENCY-1R.success_condition: on the host, witnesses FIRST: the headless court (shell latency1r-selftest, a deterministic mock surface) passes on the same build, and in the window both arms render every sealed move with the index frame equal to the session's sealed frame witness and the two arms' composites byte-identical, before any clock; then N samples per cell (2 regimes x 2 arms), interleaved in ABBA order (reversed on odd rounds), each round rendering the round's sealed frame in all four cells, every sample starting from a composition, and each sample's composite compared byte-for-byte to its pre-verified bytes after its composition, outside the interval; per cell the p50/p95/p99/max of render-start -> frame-ready (render), frame-ready -> composited (present) and render-start -> composited (total), with the measured refresh period beside them, sealed under the envelope as shell/attest/latency1r-<host>.json citing this entry. Per regime, on p50s: render delta dR = render(S) - render(P); glass delta dG = total(S) - total(P); propagation = floor(1000*dG/dR) permille. The owner chose, after PRESENT-SCALE-0 and PRESENT-STRETCH-0 had measured and deliberately not chosen: the shell shows THE CERTIFIED PICTURE, 1:1 — the kernel's 1920x1080 composite, pixel for pixel, with no reduction by GDI or by the kernel — in a BORDERLESS window covering the 1920x1080 screen at (0,0), so the whole frame is visible. No new VIEW law is needed: the picture on the screen is meant to be the picture the gate certifies. The alternatives considered and not chosen: a certified 2:1 reduction (new VIEW semantics), and a stated GDI stretch mode (uncertified pixels).
PRESENTATION-CHOICE-0.success_condition: an implementation conforms when it presents the certified composite with destination = source = 1920x1080 and no scaling at any layer the shell controls: no GDI stretch, no DPI virtualisation (the process DPI-aware, the screen's logical and physical size both 1920x1080), a borderless popup whose 1920x1080 client sits at the screen's (0,0); and when a witness shows it: the composed screen under the window, read back, equals the certified picture byte for byte. Which call implements it is PRESENT-EXACT-0's court.
PRESENTATION-CHOICE-0.failure_condition: any scaling of the certified picture on the way to the composed screen; a partially visible frame; reading this decision as a measurement or a performance result; changing LATENCY-0's frozen windows (run and playback-window, half-size, a byte-exact prefix of shell/win32.rs) to meet it — they stay as the instruments earlier courts measured; claiming the target holds on a screen that is not 1920x1080 at 100% scaling.
interpretation_limits: a semantic decision, recorded and hash-locked; it earns nothing until an implementation is measured and witnessed against it
the witness reaches the composed screen; scan-out, the panel and any display-side colour processing after composition are outside every witness
a 1920x1080 screen at 100% scaling only; another screen is a later decision
the current half-size windows do not conform and are not changed; the conforming presenter is locked after PRESENT-EXACT-0
a borderless window has no title bar: it closes by key (Alt+F4, and Esc once the presenter is locked)
PRESENTATION-CHOICE-0.instrument: none of its own: PRESENT-EXACT-0 implements and witnesses it (the screen readback). Row presentationchoice-declared keeps this entry locked.

PRESENT-EXACT-0.hypothesis: Which GDI call implements PRESENTATION-CHOICE-0, and a witness that it does — MEASURED, never assumed. In a borderless 1920x1080 window at the screen's (0,0), the process DPI-aware, ONE variable: the present call — StretchDIBits at 1:1 (destination = source) or SetDIBitsToDevice (no stretch path at all). Everything else is shared: the sealed session rendered through the adopted LoopRenderer, the same BGR bytes, the same DwmFlush barrier and QPC clock, the locked phase origin. The witness is new: the COMPOSED SCREEN under the window is read back (a screen-DC BitBlt into a 24-bit top-down DIB) and compared with the certified picture byte for byte, after clearing the window to white through a path that is neither call and reading the white back, so a call that wrote nothing cannot pass on earlier pixels. The outcome is not predicted.
PRESENT-EXACT-0.success_condition: on the host, witnesses FIRST and as a HARD GATE: the geometry verified (client 1920x1080 at screen (0,0); the screen's logical and physical size both 1920x1080); the fresh path reproduces every sealed frame witness and the loop renderer reproduces the fresh bytes; then for every sealed frame and each call: clear to white, read back white, present, read back the composed screen, equal to the certified blit bytes with zero differing bytes; any mismatch refuses the court with no record. Then the envelope render-start -> frame-ready for the two calls, interleaved ABBA in the same run after 10 warm-up rounds, 1000 samples per cell, every composite compared after its composition; after the court the last frame is read back again under each call. Sealed as shell/attest/presentexact-<host>.json citing this entry and PRESENTATION-CHOICE-0. The reading: STRETCHDIBITS CHEAPER iff p99(StretchDIBits) <= 950 permille x p99(SetDIBitsToDevice); SETDIBITSTODEVICE CHEAPER iff p99(SetDIBitsToDevice) <= 950 permille x p99(StretchDIBits); NO MATERIAL DIFFERENCE otherwise; the 50 permille is an adoption margin, a declared decision threshold, not an uncertainty. The adoption, read by the --confirm run: STRETCHDIBITS iff both runs read STRETCHDIBITS CHEAPER; otherwise SETDIBITSTODEVICE, the simpler semantics. A following patch locks the shell's 1:1 presentation to the adopted call.
PRESENT-EXACT-0.failure_condition: any readback mismatch, a stale readback after the clear, a geometry other than the target, or a witness mismatch (no number is taken); the window closing before 1000 samples per cell (no partial record); a decision read off the p50s, off a comparator sealed in another run, or off one run; a second variable changed with the call (the window, geometry, DPI awareness, session, render entry, barrier or clock); readback or clearing inside the timed interval; claiming that the pixels reach the eye unchanged, or input-to-photon; changing LATENCY-0's frozen windows; the LATENCY-0 instrument altered (its text must remain a byte-exact prefix of shell/win32.rs).
interpretation_limits: the readback is the composed screen before scan-out: the panel, the cable and display-side colour processing are outside it
the readback is taken on the sealed frames before the clock and on the last frame after it, not on every timed sample
a notification, another topmost window, a cursor capture or a colour-management transform over the window would fail the readback: the court refuses rather than measuring around it

p99 at N = 1000 is the 11th-largest sample (nearest rank); the 12 largest per call are reported beside it; the p50s, the call interval and frame-ready -> composited are reported beside, never ruled on
HOST-STATE-0's snapshots are recorded beside each run and never read by the rule
this host, this 1920x1080 screen at 100% scaling, this GPU driver only; Windows-only; off-gate on a named host; the fixed sealed reference session and the locked phase origin only

REFUSAL-WHY-0.hypothesis: Why a screen readback refused — EXPLANATORY APPARATUS, never a correctness dependency. PRESENT-EXACT-0's first host run refused READBACK-STALE and only a separate probe and the owner's knowledge named the cause (a vendor's real-time monitor overlay). REFUSAL-WHY-0 appends an attribution to every screen-readback refusal and mismatch message AFTER its verdict is decided: the bounding box of the differing pixels, then the top-level windows above ours in the Z order that are visible, not cloaked, and whose rectangles meet the box — each with its owning program's image name, process id, class, title, rectangle and the extended styles an overlay usually carries (topmost, layered, click-through, tool window, no-activate). If none meets the box it says the cause is below the window layer. It reads the window list and each owner's image name and changes nothing. The question is attribution only: a refusal names candidates; a candidate is not a cause.
REFUSAL-WHY-0.success_condition: every PRESENTEXACT-READBACK and PRESENTEXACT-READBACK-STALE refusal, every mismatch line of shell show and show-playback, and the probe's screen line carry the attribution after the decided text; the decision — the refusal code, the exit status and the counted differing bytes — is computed before the attribution is called and does not read it; the attribution's box is the box the message already describes; the attribution calls read-only window and process queries only; the trait's default names nothing, so a surface without an attribution keeps its message unchanged; on every gate the mock court's planted refusals (a changed byte, a clear that writes nothing) still refuse with no record and carry the mock's attribution after the decision.
REFUSAL-WHY-0.failure_condition: any verdict, refusal code, exit status or count that depends on the attribution; the attribution called before the decision; any call that moves, shows, hides, activates, closes, messages or terminates another window or process (SetWindowPos, ShowWindow, PostMessage, SendMessage, SetForegroundWindow, BringWindowToTop, MoveWindow, DestroyWindow on another window, TerminateProcess); a court that retries, waits out or measures around a named window; a claim that a named window caused the difference (a candidate, never a cause); the attribution entering a sealed record or a rule.
interpretation_limits: the Z order and the rectangles are read after the readback, not at its instant: a window that moved, appeared or closed in between can be missed or named wrongly

only top-level windows are walked; child windows, the cursor, compositor-level overlays, colour transforms and pixels drawn outside any window are not named — 'below the window layer' is where the walk stops, not a diagnosis
an owner the process cannot query with limited rights (elevated or protected) reads as unreadable
at most six windows are named per box; a named window is a candidate, never a cause
no number is produced: this entry locks a method of explanation, not a measurement

Rows refusalwhy-preregistered and refusalwhy-fence.

HOST-STATE-1.hypothesis: Whether a cross-run drift can be set beside a change in the clock the OS reports or in paging — RECORDED, never controlled: HOST-STATE-0's apparatus extended by two fields, an apparatus and not an optimization. HOST-STATE-0's MHz is CallNtPowerInformation's and it records nothing about paging, while the 40-60% cross-run drifts sat beside memory pressure with no paging witness. HOST-STATE-1 is version 2 of the snapshot: HOST-STATE-0's fields unchanged and in order, then clock (the performance counters \Processor Information(_Total)\Processor Frequency, % Processor Performance and % Processor Utility, uncapped, over a 1000 ms window, and an effective-MHz estimate = nominal x performance) and faults (\Memory\Page Faults/sec, Page Reads/sec and Pages Input/sec over a 1000 ms window), read through pdh.dll by their English names. Version 1 stays the default everywhere, so no court that cites HOST-STATE-0 changes what it records. The question is association only.
HOST-STATE-1.success_condition: a version 2 snapshot records HOST-STATE-0's registered fields in order, then clock and faults, each captured or marked unavailable with its reason, each counter on its own (a counter that cannot be added or formatted is unavailable with its PDH status and the others stand), integers and strings only (percentages as rounded permille, rates as rounded per-second integers); capture(version=1) is HOST-STATE-0's snapshot unchanged and is the default of capture, capture_safe and diagcommon.host_run; capture_safe never raises for either version; validate accepts exactly the two registered shapes; python verify/hoststate.py prints a version 2 look and writes nothing. A court records version 2 only when its own preregistered entry says so.
HOST-STATE-1.failure_condition: any control of the host; a version 1 snapshot changed; a court that cites HOST-STATE-0 recording version 2; any rule reading host state; a float or a boolean in a snapshot; treating the effective-MHz estimate or % Processor Performance as a measured clock; reading a system-wide paging rate as the court's own; a claim that a recorded state caused, explains or corrects a number (association, never cause).
interpretation_limits: the counters as the OS computes them: % Processor Performance is the OS's ratio of delivered to nominal clock averaged over the window and every processor, not a measured frequency, and the estimate inherits that
each window is 1000 ms of the whole system around the snapshot, not the court's own interval; a version 2 snapshot holds three such windows in turn (load, clock, faults), about three seconds
the paging rates are system-wide: page reads are the hard faults of every process
thermal state is still not captured
a recorded coincidence is not a cause: HOST-STATE-1 can make a drift explainable, never explained
HOST-STATE-1.instrument: verify/hoststate.py: FIELDS (HOST-STATE-0, version 1, unchanged) and FIELDS_V2 (version 2), capture(version=...), clock() and faults() over _pdh (PdhOpenQueryW, PdhAddEnglishCounterW, PdhCollectQueryData twice a window apart, PdhGetFormattedCounterValue with PDH_FMT_DOUBLE | PDH_FMT_NOCAP100, PdhCloseQuery), validate accepting versions 1 and 2, capture_safe(version=...); python verify/hoststate.py prints a version 2 look. Rows hoststate1-preregistered and hoststate1-record.

REFUSAL-LOG-0.hypothesis: Whether refusals on the present path recur — an OBSERVATION, never evidence and never authority. A console line says that a refusal happened, once; nothing keeps it, so a refusal that recurs across runs can only be recalled from transcripts. REFUSAL-LOG-0 appends one unsealed line per refusal event on the admitted present-path operations to an append-only log: the PRESENT-EXACT-0 court (every refusal it returns, logged where it is emitted, by the headless selftest and by the host window) and the locked presenter (shell show and show-playback: every refusal, and every completed screen readback whose pixels differ from the presented certified frame, one record each). A record carries refusal_id, run_id, a monotonic seq within the run, unix_ms, operation, surface, reason_code (the refusal's stable console code), attribution (where on the path it came from, as a fixed token from a registered vocabulary such as present.readback, never a prose diagnosis), a small context of integers and strings, and context_digest (the sha256 of the context's JSON). The log is written beside the refusal and never read back by anything on the path; it is not sealed, not chained and not committed. The question is recurrence only: counts by reason and attribution across runs. A count is not a cause, and zero is not proof that a refusal cannot occur.
REFUSAL-LOG-0.success_condition: every refusal event emitted by an admitted operation produces exactly one record, and every record corresponds to exactly one emitted refusal: on every gate the mock court's clean run adds no record and each of its six plants (a tampered witness, a mid-court close, the geometry, a changed byte, a call that writes nothing, a clear that writes nothing) adds exactly one, whose reason_code is the code the console printed, whose attribution is the registered one for that plant, and whose refusal_id is its run_id and seq; the log only grows (every earlier byte stays); without VERDANDI_REFUSAL_LOG the record goes to build/refusals.log under the working directory; a log that cannot be written is said on the console and the refusal's exit status and message are unchanged; the presenter's refusal paths print only through the logging primitive and each differing readback calls it once, after the verdict is counted; the gate points VERDANDI_REFUSAL_LOG at its own scratch file; python verify/refusallog.py validates and counts the log and writes nothing.
REFUSAL-LOG-0.failure_condition: a refusal that prints without a record, a record without a refusal, or two records for one refusal; a record rewritten, reordered or removed by the shell; a refusal's exit status, message or verdict that depends on the log; anything on the present path reading the log; the log sealed, chained, committed or cited as evidence; a network write; a rule reading the log; a count read as a cause, or zero read as proof of absence; the gate writing into the owner's log; the presenter's decisions, geometry, call or cadence changed by the instrumentation.
interpretation_limits: a refusal inside an admitted operation only: argument errors, the windowless build's refusal, and the host window court's harness (the shared DWM prelude and the window's creation, before the court function starts) are outside REFUSAL-LOG-0
the presenter's records are source-fenced, not executed on the gate: show needs a window, and the one-to-one invariant is proven executably on the court only
a failed append breaks the one-to-one invariant for that event and says so on the console; the log cannot record its own failure
unix_ms is the wall clock and run_id its start and the process id: identities for grouping, not a timing instrument
a count is an observation of this host and these runs: recurrence is not a cause, and zero records is not proof that a refusal cannot occur

Rows refusallog-preregistered, refusallog-bijection, refusallog-fence and refusallog-reader.

RUN-LEDGER-0.hypothesis: How many admitted runs there were — the DENOMINATOR the refusal log lacks, an observation, never evidence. REFUSAL-LOG-0 holds refusal events only, so a run that refused nothing leaves no trace in it, and 'no refusals occurred' cannot be told from 'the run was not recorded'. RUN-LEDGER-0 appends one unsealed line per admitted run to a separate append-only ledger, whatever its outcome, when the run ends: run_id (the refusal log's, so the two files join), operation, surface, readbacks_checked and differed (the operation's own counts of compared screen readbacks), refusals (how many refusal records the run emitted), exit_code (the code the run ends with), unix_ms_start and unix_ms_end. The admitted runs are REFUSAL-LOG-0's admitted operations: a PRESENT-EXACT-0 court run (begun just before the court function, ended with the court's outcome) and a presenter run (show and show-playback: begun on entry, ended at every exit). The ledger is not sealed, not chained, not committed, and read by no rule and by nothing on the path; the refusal log keeps only refusals. The question is exposure only: with the ledger a recurrence can be stated as refused in N of M runs. A rate is an observation of this host and these runs, not a cause.
RUN-LEDGER-0.success_condition: every admitted run appends exactly one line and every line is one admitted run: on every gate the mock court's clean run and each of its six plants append exactly one line each, with exit_code equal to the process's exit status, readbacks_checked equal to the court's own count (on the clean run, the raw record's readback checks), differed 0 on the clean run and on the plants that refuse before a presented frame differs and 1 on the changed byte and on the call that writes nothing, refusals equal to the refusal records carrying its run_id (0 clean, 1 each plant), and run_id equal to those records'; a failure before the run begins (a usage error) appends no line; the ledger only grows; without VERDANDI_RUN_LEDGER the line goes to build/runs.log under the working directory; a ledger that cannot be written is said on the console and the run's exit status and output are unchanged; the presenter begins its run on entry, ends it once immediately before each of its exits with that exit's code, and counts each compared readback where it counts its own; the gate points VERDANDI_RUN_LEDGER at its own scratch file; python verify/runledger.py validates, counts and joins the two files and writes nothing.
RUN-LEDGER-0.failure_condition: an admitted run without a line, a line without a run, or two lines for one run; a line whose exit_code, counts or refusals disagree with the run; refusal records written into the ledger or run lines into the refusal log; a line rewritten, reordered or removed by the shell; a run's exit status, output or verdict that depends on the ledger; anything on the present path reading it; the ledger sealed, chained, committed or cited as evidence; a network write; a rule reading it; a rate read as a cause, or a clean run read as proof that a refusal cannot occur; the gate writing into the owner's ledger; the presenter's decisions, geometry, call or cadence changed by the instrumentation.
interpretation_limits: a run of an admitted operation only, begun where the operation begins: argument errors, the windowless build, and the host window court's harness before the court function starts append no line
a court run's exit_code is the court's outcome (0 returned, 2 refused): a later failure to write its raw record exits 2 after a line that says 0
the presenter's lines are source-fenced, not executed on the gate: show needs a window
a process killed from outside (ended by another program, or a crash) ends without a line: the ledger undercounts such runs and cannot say so
a failed append loses that run's line and says so on the console
a rate is an observation of this host and these runs: not a cause, and a run with no refusals is not proof that a refusal cannot occur
RUN-LEDGER-0.instrument: shell/runledger.rs (begin, readback, end: one line appended when the run ends, OpenOptions append; $VERDANDI_RUN_LEDGER, else build/runs.log; the run_id and the refusal count from shell/refusallog.rs); begin and end at the court's two emission points (main.rs's selftest, win32.rs's presentexact_window) and in the presenter (on entry, and before each of its seven exits); readback where the court (witness_one) and the presenter (show_witness) count their own; verify/runledger.py (validate, read, tally, join; prints and writes nothing); verify.py sets VERDANDI_RUN_LEDGER to verify/build/runs-gate.log before any row. Rows runledger-preregistered, runledger-bijection, runledger-fence and runledger-reader.

REFUSAL-WHY-1.hypothesis: Which windows recur over the screen when a readback differs — REFUSAL-WHY-0's attribution carried into the refusal log so that it can accumulate: explanatory apparatus, never a correctness dependency. REFUSAL-WHY-0 names the windows above ours over a differing box on the console only, once. REFUSAL-WHY-1 writes the same walk's result into the refusal-log record of every screen-readback refusal of the court and of every differing readback of the presenter, after the verdict is decided and counted: the layer (windows: a window above ours meets the box; below: none does, so the cause is below the window layer; unplaced: our window was not found in the Z order), the number of windows named, and for each (at most six) its program's image name, its class, its overlay flags and its rectangle. Titles are never persisted: they may appear on the console but never enter the log; process ids are not persisted either. The rectangle is diagnostic geometry, not identity: the grouping key is program, class and flags. One walk serves both the console's words and the log's fields. The question is recurrence only: which program, class and flags recur over the screen across runs. A candidate is not a cause.
REFUSAL-WHY-1.success_condition: on every gate, over the mock court: the changed-byte, the call-that-writes-nothing and the clear-that-writes-nothing plants' records carry the layer and the count after the refusal's own context, and the refusal itself (code, attribution, exit status, message) is unchanged; a new plant, a synthetic overlay window over the changed byte, names the window's program, pid, class, title and flags on the console, and its record carries window_1_program, window_1_class, window_1_flags and window_1_rect while neither the title nor the pid appears anywhere in the log; refusals that are not screen readbacks carry no covering fields; the reader counts covering windows by layer and by program, class and flags across runs; the log's covering fields are built by one function that reads neither the title nor the pid; the host surface and the presenter take the console's words and the log's fields from the same single walk; the presenter walks once per differing readback, after it is counted and before it is recorded.
REFUSAL-WHY-1.failure_condition: a title or a pid in the refusal log; a verdict, refusal code, exit status or count that depends on the attribution; the attribution walked before the decision, or twice for one readback; the rectangle used as a grouping key; any call that acts on another window or process; a named window read as the cause; the probe writing to the log.
interpretation_limits: the Z order is read just after the readback, not at its instant: a window that moved, appeared or closed in between can be missed or named wrongly
image and class names can repeat across unrelated programs: a group is a candidate kind of overlay, not an identified one
an owner that cannot be queried with limited rights reads as unreadable, and all such owners group together
the presenter's covering fields are source-fenced, not executed on the gate: show needs a window
at most six windows per record
a count is not a cause, and zero records is not proof that a refusal cannot occur
REFUSAL-WHY-1.instrument: shell/presentexact.rs: Seen, Seeing, Attribution, seen_text (the console's words, REFUSAL-WHY-0's format), seen_context (the log's fields: layer, count, and program, class, flags and rectangle per window; never a title or a pid), ExactSurface::attribute returning both from one walk, why() appending the fields after the refusal's own context; the mock's plant "overlay" (a synthetic covering window with a title); shell/win32.rs's REFUSAL-WHY section: covering (the one walk), covering_windows (the probe's words only); the presenter's show_witness walks once per differing readback after the count, its fields in the record and its words in the printed line; verify/refusallog.py counts covering windows. Rows refusalwhy1-preregistered, refusalwhy1-log and refusalwhy1-fence.
